statement: The contact's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ...}; src=mapping.get(name,name)
alternative: The contract validates account_id against raw.account, and raw.contact has a separate account_id column: "account_id IN (SELECT id FROM raw.account)".
reason: This mapping replaces account relationships for every retained contact.

statement: The opportunity's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ...}; src=mapping.get(name,name)
alternative: The contract validates account_id against raw.account, and raw.opportunity has a distinct account_id column.
reason: Every opportunity's account relationship depends on this interpretation.

statement: The user's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id, contact_id, and user_role_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ... 'contact_id':'id', ... 'user_role_id':'id'}
alternative: raw.user contains separate account_id, contact_id, and user_role_id columns corresponding to the contract's columns.
reason: The global mapping replaces three different user relationships with the user's identity.

statement: The line item's own raw id is the intended source for its opportunity_id and product_2_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={... 'opportunity_id':'id', ... 'product_2_id':'id', ...}
alternative: raw.opportunity_line_item exposes distinct opportunity_id and product_2_id columns, which the contract also names.
reason: Both principal relationships of every line item depend on this mapping.

statement: The order's own raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ...}; src=mapping.get(name,name)
alternative: The inspected raw.order_data schema contains a distinct account_id column.
reason: This changes the account association of every generated order.

statement: The contact history record's raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ... 'contact_id':'id', ...}
alternative: raw.contact_history has a separate account_id column in addition to id.
reason: Historical contact-to-account relationships are replaced throughout the output.

statement: The opportunity history record's raw id is the intended source for its account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: mapping={'account_id':'id', ... 'opportunity_id':'id', ...}
alternative: raw.opportunity_history has a separate account_id column in addition to id.
reason: Historical opportunity-to-account relationships depend on this mapping.

statement: Only one history version per account needs to be retained to satisfy history_unique_key uniqueness.
evidence_of_dependence: 'history_unique_key':'id'; qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
alternative: The contract describes "account history records tracking changes to account data over time" and declares history_unique_key, rather than account_id, unique.
reason: Deduplicating by entity id can discard nearly all historical versions.

statement: Only one history version per contact needs to be retained to satisfy history_unique_key uniqueness.
evidence_of_dependence: 'history_unique_key':'id'; qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
alternative: The contract describes "contact history records tracking changes to contact data over time" and requires history_unique_key to be unique.
reason: Entity-level deduplication can remove most contact history.

statement: The opportunity's six derived timing columns can be read directly from raw.opportunity without computation.
evidence_of_dependence: src=mapping.get(name,name); selects.append(f'    {expr} as {name}')
alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity schema lacks is_created_this_month, is_created_this_quarter, days_since_created, days_to_close, is_closed_this_month, and is_closed_this_quarter, although the contract requires them.
reason: The generated model depends on unavailable source expressions for required output columns.

statement: The contact created_date can be sourced directly as created_date from raw.contact.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
alternative: The complete DESCRIBE raw.contact output contains no created_date column.
reason: This required output expression depends on a source column absent from the inspected schema.

statement: The opportunity history last_modified_date can be read directly from raw.opportunity_history.
evidence_of_dependence: src=mapping.get(name,name); expr=f'try_cast({expr} as {typ})'
alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity_history schema lacks last_modified_date but includes _fivetran_synced and _fivetran_start.
reason: The model requires a source expression not present in the inspected table.

statement: Contact foreign-key validation is unnecessary for owner_id and reports_to_id.
evidence_of_dependence: The contact filters contain only id checks and 'not coalesce(is_deleted, false)', while owner_id and reports_to_id are projected directly.
alternative: The contract requires invalid owner_id and reports_to_id values to be nullified using both ID-format checks and membership in raw.user or raw.contact.
reason: Unvalidated relationships can propagate unusable identifiers downstream.

statement: The contact phone, photo_url, email-independent required-name, and birthdate fields already satisfy their contract checks without additional processing.
evidence_of_dependence: The generator applies contact-specific cleaning only to email and filters only id and is_deleted.
alternative: The contract requires phone and photo_url trimming and length checks, birthdate bounds, and not-null last_name and contact_name.
reason: Several explicitly required contact quality controls are omitted.

statement: All opportunity close_date values already satisfy the contract's historical, future, and creation-date bounds.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('close_date','birthdate','start_date_time','end_date_time'): pass
alternative: The contract requires nullification outside 1900 through CURRENT_DATE plus one year or before created_date.
reason: Unchecked dates affect both pipeline reporting and sales-cycle calculations.

statement: All opportunity owner_id values already satisfy the required format and raw.user membership checks.
evidence_of_dependence: The opportunity filter list checks id, deletion, and name but not owner_id.
alternative: The contract requires invalid owner_id values to be nullified after format and raw.user membership validation.
reason: Invalid owner references can alter attribution and enrichment.

statement: Deleted opportunity line items may remain in staging.
evidence_of_dependence: if n=='stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item': filters=['id is not null']
alternative: The contract specifies "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)" with on_failure: delete_row.
reason: Retaining deleted line items can inflate downstream product and revenue analysis.

statement: All retained events already satisfy end_date_time being no earlier than start_date_time.
evidence_of_dependence: if n=='stg_salesforce__event': filters=['id is not null','owner_id is not null']
alternative: The contract requires delete_row when "end_date_time IS NULL OR end_date_time >= start_date_time" fails.
reason: The required rejection of temporally invalid events is absent.

statement: Event start and end timestamps already satisfy their contract range limits.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('close_date','birthdate','start_date_time','end_date_time'): pass
alternative: The contract requires nullification outside 2000–2100 and additionally limits start_date_time to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP plus one year.
reason: Out-of-range calendar values would survive unchanged.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary raw row for each user id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Conflicting duplicate users can produce nondeterministic attributes and relationships.

statement: Deduplicating users by user_id alone is sufficient to guarantee username uniqueness.
evidence_of_dependence: key=...get(unique[0]); partition by {key}
alternative: The contract declares both user_id and username "[not_null, unique]".
reason: Different user ids sharing a username are not addressed by the generated deduplication.

statement: The status whitelist should be applied to raw lead status before any trimming.
evidence_of_dependence: 'status in (\'Open - Not Contacted\', \'Working - Contacted\', \'Closed - Converted\', \'Closed - Not Converted\')'
alternative: The contract specifies "status = TRIM(status)" with on_failure: correct, supporting correction of whitespace before validation.
reason: Otherwise-correct leads with padded statuses would be removed rather than repaired.

statement: Every retained lead already has a non-null owner_id.
evidence_of_dependence: The lead filter list checks id, last_name, name, and status but not owner_id.
alternative: The contract declares lead owner_id "constraints: [not_null]".
reason: The model relies on source cleanliness to satisfy an explicit required field.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per lead id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Conflicting versions can change status and conversion attributes without a defined selection rule.

statement: The status whitelist should be applied to raw task status before any trimming.
evidence_of_dependence: 'status in (\'Not Started\', \'In Progress\', \'Completed\', \'Waiting on someone else\', \'Deferred\')'
alternative: The contract specifies "status = TRIM(status)" with on_failure: correct.
reason: Padded valid statuses would cause entire tasks to be discarded.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per task id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Conflicting duplicate tasks can change completion and activity reporting.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per event id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Conflicting event versions can produce different dates and ownership.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per user role id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Duplicate role versions could disagree on hierarchy or role name.

statement: Keeping an arbitrary row per product id is an acceptable duplicate-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over (partition by {key} order by {key}) = 1
reason: Conflicting product versions can change catalog classifications and active status.

statement: The account history created_date represents the Fivetran version start timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
reason: Version validity time and business creation time have different analytical meanings.

statement: The contact history created_date represents the Fivetran version start timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
reason: Historical analyses depend on the intended meaning of this timestamp.

statement: The opportunity history created_date should use _fivetran_start rather than the source created_date.
evidence_of_dependence: if name in ('created_date',) and n.endswith('_history'): expr='_fivetran_start'
alternative: The inspected raw.opportunity_history schema includes a distinct created_date column.
reason: Replacing business creation time with version start can change historical sales-cycle calculations.

statement: Entity id plus _fivetran_start and _fivetran_end is sufficient to identify each opportunity history row.
evidence_of_dependence: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast({keyid} as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_start as varchar), ''), coalesce(cast(_fivetran_end as varchar), '')))
reason: Different versions with identical identity inputs would receive the same generated key.

statement: Null entity ids should cause account history rows to be removed.
evidence_of_dependence: if n=='stg_salesforce__account_history': filters=['id is not null']
alternative: The account history contract requires history_unique_key to be non-null but does not declare account_id non-null.
reason: This adds a row-exclusion policy beyond the explicit history constraints.

statement: Non-deleted staging accounts have at most one row per account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: from account_base ... select * from account_derived
reason: Without deduplication, repeated account IDs violate the required grain and can multiply downstream opportunity rows.

statement: Accounts with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included as non-deleted accounts and have their output flag set to FALSE.
evidence_of_dependence: where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) ... coalesce(is_deleted, false) as is_deleted
alternative: The intermediate contract says "keep only rows where is_deleted is false", while the staging contract permits NULL deletion flags through "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)".
reason: This interpretation expands the account population beyond a strict FALSE filter.

statement: Opportunities with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included as non-deleted opportunities and have their output flag set to FALSE.
evidence_of_dependence: where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) ... coalesce(op.is_deleted, false) as is_deleted
alternative: The intermediate contract specifies "filtered to is_deleted = false", while staging permits NULL flags through "NOT COALESCE(is_deleted, false)".
reason: Including NULL-flag opportunities can change pipeline counts and monetary totals.

statement: The staging account table contains at most one matching row per active account_id.
evidence_of_dependence: select account_id from staging.stg_salesforce__account ... left join staging.stg_salesforce__account s on a.account_id = s.account_id
reason: Duplicate IDs can multiply rows through both the account set and the second account join, violating the required grain.

statement: Accounts with a NULL is_deleted flag belong in the activity summary's active account population.
evidence_of_dependence: select account_id from staging.stg_salesforce__account where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
alternative: The contract defines the output population as accounts "where is_deleted=false".
reason: This changes which accounts receive summary rows.

statement: Tasks with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to activity metrics.
evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__task where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
alternative: The contract says to keep task rows "where is_deleted=false".
reason: These additional tasks can change activity counts, recency, owner counts, and engagement defaults.

statement: Events with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to activity metrics.
evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__event where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
alternative: The contract says to keep event rows "where is_deleted=false".
reason: These additional events can change activity counts, recency, owner counts, and engagement defaults.

statement: Leads with a NULL is_deleted flag should be included in the lead conversion funnel.
evidence_of_dependence: select * from staging.stg_salesforce__lead where not coalesce(is_deleted, false)
alternative: The contract says "include only leads where is_deleted = false" and describes all output rows as having "is_deleted=false".
reason: This expands the funnel population and allows NULL deletion flags into its output.

statement: Passing through annual_revenue as DECIMAL(18,3) is acceptable for the funnel's required DECIMAL(18,2) output.
evidence_of_dependence: annual_revenue, number_of_employees, is_converted, conversion_time_days
alternative: The staging contract declares annual_revenue as "DECIMAL(18,3)", while the funnel column declares "DECIMAL(18,2)".
reason: Without an explicit conversion, the output retains a different monetary scale from the declared schema.

statement: A converted identifier is considered present whenever it is non-NULL, even if it is an empty or whitespace-only string.
evidence_of_dependence: converted_account_id is not null and converted_contact_id is not null and converted_opportunity_id is not null
alternative: The contract requires all three converted IDs to be "present", which could instead require nonempty identifiers.
reason: The interpretation determines whether leads with blank conversion references are marked complete.

statement: Leads with a NULL is_deleted flag should contribute to user performance metrics.
evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__lead where not coalesce(is_deleted, false) and owner_id is not null group by owner_id
alternative: The contract describes total_leads as the "Count of non-deleted leads owned by the user", and the lead funnel explicitly uses "is_deleted = false" for non-deleted leads.
reason: Including unknown deletion states changes lead totals, converted totals, and conversion rates.

statement: Each retained staging opportunity row represents a distinct opportunity for user-level counting.
evidence_of_dependence: count(*) as total_opportunities
reason: Repeated opportunity records would inflate counts and sums and could change performance tiers.

statement: BIGINT counts are acceptable for won_opportunities and converted_leads despite their declared HUGEINT output types.
evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter (where is_won = true) as won_opportunities; count(*) filter (where is_converted = true) as converted_leads
alternative: The contract declares both won_opportunities and converted_leads as "HUGEINT".
reason: The count expressions and subsequent coalescing do not explicitly produce the contracted types.

statement: Joining opportunities to accounts is unnecessary for the owner aggregation.
evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity o left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on o.owner_id=u.user_id
alternative: The business logic explicitly requires "Opportunity to Account on account_id"; account matches could also multiply opportunity rows because account_id uniqueness has not been established.
reason: Omitting the prescribed account join can change every aggregate if accounts have multiple matching rows.

statement: An owner's manager_id may be reported directly without resolving it to a matching staging user.
evidence_of_dependence: select o.*, u.manager_id
alternative: The contract requires joining "Owner.manager_id to User (manager)", which supports using the resolved manager user's identifier rather than an unmatched reference.
reason: Unresolved manager references can populate manager fields and affect precedence instead of remaining null.

statement: Rounding decimal sums without casting them to DECIMAL(38,0) satisfies the declared aggregate output types.
evidence_of_dependence: round(sum(amount)) as total_bookings_amount; round(sum(weighted_amount)) as total_pipeline_forecast_amount
alternative: The contract declares monetary sum columns such as total_bookings_amount and total_pipeline_forecast_amount as "DECIMAL(38,0)", whereas rounding alone need not produce that declared scale.
reason: Numerically rounded values can still have a schema different from the required output types.

statement: Joining the owner to the user-role table is unnecessary to satisfy this model's prescribed processing and dependencies.
evidence_of_dependence: The enhanced_opportunity CTE joins only staging.stg_salesforce__user to the opportunity source.
alternative: The contract lists staging.stg_salesforce__user_role as a source model and explicitly requires joining "Owner.user_role_id to User Role".
reason: The implementation omits an explicitly prescribed upstream join even though no role attributes are projected.

statement: Defaulting missing activity values before calculating engagement metrics is equivalent to applying defaults only in the final projection.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(acs.activity_trend_30d,'New') as activity_trend_30d ... from engagement_base
alternative: The contract says "Apply defaults to activity fields in the final projection" and specifies that NULL scoring components fall to their else buckets; a NULL trend contributes 0 rather than the 5 points assigned to 'New'.
reason: Missing activity matches can receive different health scores and lifecycle classifications because defaults are applied before business rules.

statement: The staged user_name value is interchangeable with the required trimmed concatenation of first_name and last_name for account owner names.
evidence_of_dependence: u.user_name as owner_name
alternative: The contract requires owner_name to be built "by concatenating first and last name with a space and trimming".
reason: Every matched account owner name depends on an unverified equivalence between separate user attributes.

statement: A closed opportunity with NULL is_won should be classified as Lost.
evidence_of_dependence: when is_closed and not coalesce(is_won,false) then 'Lost'
alternative: The contract specifies "Lost if is_closed and not is_won" and "otherwise Unknown", under which a NULL is_won does not satisfy the Lost condition.
reason: Treating unknown win status as false changes the classification of affected closed opportunities.

statement: An opportunity with NULL opportunity_age_days should receive the Long Cycle category.
evidence_of_dependence: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then 'Extended' else 'Long Cycle' end
alternative: The contract describes Long Cycle as ">180 days", while the upstream opportunity contract explicitly permits NULL age when created_date is missing.
reason: The fallback assigns a duration category to opportunities whose duration is unknown.

statement: The opportunity model may generate a new load timestamp instead of preserving the staging model's load timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(current_timestamp as timestamp with time zone) as _dbt_loaded_at
alternative: The contract describes this column as "Model load timestamp from stg_salesforce__opportunity" and requires "emit all source columns as-is".
reason: The generated timestamp describes the mart execution rather than the upstream load.

statement: A NULL is_closed value must not qualify an opportunity as Pipeline in the enhanced model.
evidence_of_dependence: when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
alternative: The contract's status column description says "Pipeline if is_closed is not true", and its is_closed description says "NULL treated as not closed in status derivation"; however, another passage says NULL booleans result in Other.
reason: The implementation chooses one side of conflicting NULL-status requirements.

statement: The daily opportunity history status rules apply independently of NULL values in inputs not needed by the matching branch.
evidence_of_dependence: case when is_won is true then 'Won' ... when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
alternative: The contract also states "If is_won, is_closed, or forecast_category is NULL, none of the first three conditions apply and status is Other".
reason: Rows with partially missing status inputs can receive Won, Lost, or Pipeline instead of Other.

statement: Passing through INTEGER timing fields satisfies the enhanced opportunity model's BIGINT timing-field requirements.
evidence_of_dependence: is_created_this_month,is_created_this_quarter,days_since_created,days_to_close,is_closed_this_month
alternative: The staging contract declares days_since_created and days_to_close as INTEGER, while the enhanced model declares both as BIGINT.
reason: Direct projection retains the upstream types rather than producing the declared mart schema.

statement: The staging contact table contains at most one row for each contact_id.
evidence_of_dependence: select c.* ... from staging.stg_salesforce__contact c
reason: Repeated source contact IDs would violate the mart's unique contact_id test even without join multiplication.

statement: Retained staging line items have unique opportunity_line_item_id values.
evidence_of_dependence: from staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity_line_item oli
alternative: The mart requires "One row per opportunity_line_item_id" and a unique test, but the staging contract does not declare this identifier unique.
reason: Duplicate base identifiers would violate the required output grain even without join multiplication.

statement: The staging opportunity table has at most one matching row per opportunity_id.
evidence_of_dependence: left join staging.stg_salesforce__opportunity opp on oli.opportunity_id=opp.opportunity_id
reason: Multiple matching opportunity rows would multiply line items and their downstream measures.

statement: The line-item status rules may match a branch even when another status input is NULL.
evidence_of_dependence: case when is_won is true then 'Won' ... when is_closed is false and lower(forecast_category) in ('pipeline','forecast','bestcase') then 'Pipeline'
alternative: The contract also says "Any NULL in is_won, is_closed, or forecast_category prevents a match and defaults to 'Other'".
reason: Partially missing inputs can produce Won, Lost, or Pipeline instead of Other.

statement: Every retained staging line item has a non-null opportunity_line_item_id.
evidence_of_dependence: select opportunity_line_item_id ... from line_items
alternative: The mart specifies "NULLs not allowed", whereas the staging column has no not-null constraint.
reason: The mart performs no additional identifier validation to enforce its required key.

statement: A close day containing won opportunities whose amounts are all NULL should report zero opportunities_won_amount.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(round(sum(amount) filter(where deal_status='Won')),0) as opportunities_won_amount
alternative: The contract specifies zero "when there are close_day records but none Won" and says that amounts may be NULL and are used in sums; it does not explicitly extend that zero default to won rows with entirely missing amounts.
reason: The coalescing conflates absent won opportunities with won opportunities whose monetary values are unknown.

statement: Rounding daily monetary sums without explicitly casting them satisfies the required DECIMAL(38,0) output schema.
evidence_of_dependence: round(sum(amount)) as opportunities_created_amount
alternative: The contract declares opportunities_created_amount, opportunities_won_amount, opportunities_lost_amount, and pipeline_amount as "DECIMAL(38,0)".
reason: Numerically integral results do not by themselves establish the required decimal precision and scale.

statement: A closed opportunity with NULL is_won should count as lost in the sales snapshot.
evidence_of_dependence: is_closed is true and is_won is not true
alternative: The snapshot contract defines lost opportunities as "closed and not won" and says conditional counts include only rows where the condition is true; a literal Boolean NOT of NULL would not qualify.
reason: Treating unknown win status as not won changes lost counts, lost value, and the close rate.

statement: The staging creation-period flags identify exactly the opportunities created in the execution date's current month and quarter.
evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter(where is_created_this_month is true); sum(case when is_created_this_quarter is true then amount else 0 end)
reason: The snapshot relies entirely on upstream flags rather than checking created_date against its execution-time context.

statement: The staging closure-period flags identify exactly the closed opportunities whose close dates fall in the execution date's current month and quarter.
evidence_of_dependence: is_won is true and is_closed_this_month is true
reason: These metrics never independently verify either closed status or the close-date period.

statement: A closed opportunity with NULL opportunity_age_days should receive a Long Cycle Win or Long Cycle Loss velocity category.
evidence_of_dependence: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then 'Extended Win (91-180d)' else 'Long Cycle Win (>180d)' end
alternative: The contract defines long-cycle categories as ">180" days, while opportunity_age_days is explicitly nullable when created_date is missing.
reason: Missing durations are classified as known long cycles rather than remaining unclassified.

statement: The manager performance result does not need to be ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending.
evidence_of_dependence: from manager_rollup r left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on r.manager_id=u.user_id
alternative: The contract requires "the final result is ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending".
reason: The omitted ordering affects the explicitly prescribed result presentation but not metric values.

statement: A NULL quarter-over-quarter revenue growth rate should contribute 10 points to the team health score.
evidence_of_dependence: when coalesce(revenue_growth_qoq_percentage,0)>=-10 then 10 else 5 end
alternative: The contract specifies "20 if > 10%, else 15 if > 0%, else 10 if ≥ -10%, else 5" and permits NULL growth when previous-quarter revenue is zero or NULL.
reason: Teams without a measurable growth rate receive five additional health points.

statement: Ordinary equality is sufficient to match performer-name groups when team_type is NULL.
evidence_of_dependence: left join performer_names pn using(team_manager_id,team_manager_name,team_type)
alternative: The contract explicitly says "team_type = user_type (can be null)" and requires performer names for each group.
reason: NULL team types cannot match through the equality join, losing both performer names for affected teams.

statement: A negative previous-quarter revenue total should yield NULL quarter-over-quarter growth.
evidence_of_dependence: case when team_revenue_previous_quarter>0 then round((team_revenue_current_quarter-team_revenue_previous_quarter)::double/team_revenue_previous_quarter*100,2) end
alternative: The contract specifies growth as the percentage change and says it is "null if previous-quarter revenue is zero or null", not negative.
reason: Negative revenue baselines would suppress a required growth value and alter health scoring.

statement: Closed-opportunity won revenue is the intended ranking measure for top_revenue_performer rather than the user's total_won_amount.
evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,total_revenue_won) filter(where total_revenue_won is not null)
alternative: The contract specifies "the full_name of the member with the highest total won amount"; member_metrics also selects p.total_won_amount, whose upstream definition counts opportunities marked won without requiring closed status.
reason: The two revenue measures can rank team members differently.

statement: Teams whose members all lack a ranking measure should have no top performer instead of selecting an arbitrary member.
evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,win_rate_percentage) filter(where win_rate_percentage is not null)
alternative: The contract says "members without a value are ranked last; ties are arbitrary", which supports retaining such members as candidates even when all values are missing.
reason: Filtering missing measures removes every candidate in all-missing teams.

statement: The opportunity closure-period flags should depend only on close_date, without requiring is_closed to be true.
evidence_of_dependence: (close_date is not null and year(close_date)=year(current_date) and month(close_date)=month(current_date)) as is_closed_this_month
alternative: The names "is_closed_this_month" and "is_closed_this_quarter" support requiring an actually closed opportunity, rather than merely a scheduled close date in the period.
reason: Open opportunities scheduled to close this period can be treated as closed-period opportunities by downstream metrics.

statement: Setting created_date to NULL for every contact is an acceptable way to populate the required contact timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: replace('try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP) as created_date','cast(null as TIMESTAMP) as created_date')
reason: The missing raw column is established, but the contract does not establish that all contact creation timestamps should therefore be discarded rather than sourced elsewhere.

statement: Setting last_modified_date to NULL for every opportunity history row is acceptable under the contract.
evidence_of_dependence: replace('last_modified_date as last_modified_date','cast(null as timestamp) as last_modified_date')
reason: Absence of the identically named raw column does not establish the intended treatment of available history timestamps.

statement: days_to_close should measure the creation-to-close-date interval for open opportunities as well as closed opportunities.
evidence_of_dependence: case when close_date is not null and created_date is not null then date_diff('day', created_date::date, close_date::date) end as days_to_close
reason: The contract lists the field without defining whether it represents a completed sales cycle, a scheduled cycle, or remaining time to close.

statement: The creation-period flags should use calendar months and quarters evaluated on the pipeline execution date.
